tickets.title: People can ask for a password reset link
tickets.summary: Anyone who forgot their password can type their email on the login page and get a reset link by email, instead of having to contact support.
tickets.story: Priya hasn't logged in for months and her password doesn't work. She clicks **Forgot password?**, types her email, and a minute later there's an email from Acme with a button to reset it.
tickets.visual:
```
 Priya (on the login page)        Acme app                               Priya's inbox
  │                                │                                       │
  │  clicks "Forgot password?" ──▶ │                                       │
  │  types priya@example.com ────▶ │── makes a one-time link (30 minutes) ─▶│  "Reset your Acme password"
  │  ◀── "Check your email" ────── │                                       │
  │                                │                                       │
  │  opens the email, clicks the link ─────────────────────────────────────┘
  │  ─────────────────────────────▶│  checks the link is fresh and unused
  │  ◀── "Choose a new password" ──│
```

The same message is shown whether or not the email belongs to an account, so nobody can use
this page to find out who has an Acme account.
tickets.description:
Adds a **Forgot password?** link under the login form. It opens a small page with one box for an email address and a *Send link* button.

### What's in
- The page, the button, and the email with the link.
- The link works for 30 minutes.

### What's out
- Choosing the new password (that is ACME-004).
- Limits on how often you can ask (that is ACME-008).
acceptance: The login page has a 'Forgot password?' link
After sending, the page says 'Check your email' whatever address was typed
An email with a reset link arrives for a known address
No email is sent for an address with no account
test_scenarios: When a known email is submitted, then one reset email is sent to it
When an unknown email is submitted, then no email is sent and the same message is shown
When the email box is empty, then the page asks for an email and sends nothing

tickets.title: The reset email is clear and easy to trust
tickets.summary: The reset email looks like it really comes from Acme and says in plain words what to do, so people aren't worried it's a scam.
tickets.story: Sam gets the email on his phone. It has the Acme logo, says who asked for it and when, and has one big 'Choose a new password' button. He knows it's real and taps the button.
tickets.visual:
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  [Acme logo]                             │
│                                          │
│  Hi Sam,                                 │
│  Someone asked to reset your password    │
│  at 10:42 today.                         │
│                                          │
│      [ Choose a new password ]           │
│                                          │
│  Didn't ask? You can ignore this email.  │
│  The link stops working in 30 minutes.   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
tickets.description:
Designs the email people get after asking for a reset.

> Most people decide in two seconds whether an email is real. The logo, their name and one clear button do most of the work.

It must read well on a phone and in dark mode email apps.
acceptance: The email shows the Acme logo and the person's first name
It says when the reset was asked for
There is exactly one button, and it opens the reset page
It says what to do if you didn't ask for it
test_scenarios: When the email is created for Sam, then it contains his first name and the time of the request
When the email is created, then it has exactly one link and it points to the reset page

tickets.description:
The page opened by the link in the reset email.

| What you do | What you see |
|---|---|
| Open a fresh link | 'Choose a new password for *your email*' |
| Type two passwords that don't match | 'The two passwords don't match' |
| Save a good password | 'Your password has been changed' |
| Open a link older than 30 minutes | 'This link has expired' and a button to send a new one |

> Open question: should saving also log you in? That is split out as ACME-006 so this ticket stays small.
acceptance: A fresh link opens the page and shows the account's email
Saving a new password changes it; the old one stops working
Mismatched passwords are caught before saving
An expired link shows a friendly message and a way to get a new one
test_scenarios: When a fresh link is opened, then the page shows the account's email
When a new password is saved, then logging in with the old password fails
When the two passwords differ, then nothing is saved and a message is shown
When a link older than 30 minutes is opened, then the expired message is shown

tickets.title: Old or already-used links stop working
tickets.summary: A reset link works once and only for 30 minutes, so an old email in someone's inbox can't be used to take over the account.
tickets.story: Months later, someone finds an old Acme reset email in Priya's inbox and clicks it. The page says the link has expired; nothing changes.
tickets.description:
Makes sure each link is used at most once and never after 30 minutes.

Asking for a new link also cancels any older links for the same account.
acceptance: A link can be used once; the second time it says it has already been used
A link older than 30 minutes says it has expired
Asking for a new link cancels the older ones
test_scenarios: When a link is used a second time, then it is refused
When a link is 31 minutes old, then it is refused
When a new link is asked for, then the previous link for that account is refused

tickets.title: Too many reset requests in a row are slowed down
tickets.summary: If someone asks for lots of reset emails very quickly, the app waits before sending more, so nobody's inbox gets flooded.
tickets.story: A prankster types Sam's email into the reset page twenty times. Sam gets one email; the prankster sees 'Please wait a few minutes before trying again'.
tickets.description: At most 3 reset emails per address per hour, and at most 20 requests per hour from one network address. The message shown never reveals whether the email has an account.
acceptance: A 4th request for the same email within an hour sends no email
The person asking sees 'Please wait a few minutes before trying again'
Limits reset after an hour
test_scenarios: When 4 requests for one email arrive within an hour, then only 3 emails are sent
When 21 requests come from one network address within an hour, then the 21st is refused
tickets.technical: Counters in Redis with a 1-hour expiry; config keys `RESET_PER_EMAIL`, `RESET_PER_IP`.

handoff.note: Built and tested; ready for review.
